# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project overview

"Sistema de Inventarios y Ventas" (Ita Flores) — a point-of-sale, inventory, and sales-history web app for a multi-branch clothing store. Originally generated by Figma Make as a frontend-only SPA; it now has a real (dev-only) backend: a Vite middleware (`server/db.mjs`) backed by MariaDB. All application data (users, products, sales, commission tiers, store logo) lives in a single React Context on the frontend, sourced from and persisted to that database via `GET`/`PUT /api/state` — not `localStorage`.

## Commands

```bash
npm i          # install dependencies (pnpm-workspace.yaml is present, but package.json scripts assume npm/vite directly)
npm run dev    # start Vite dev server
npm run build  # production build (vite build)
```

There are no lint, typecheck, or test scripts configured in `package.json` — none exist in this repo yet.

## Architecture

### Single-file application core

Nearly the entire app — types, constants, seed/mock data, persistence, context, generic UI primitives (`Btn`, `Input`, `Select`, `Modal`, `Badge`, etc.), and all feature views — lives in one file: [src/app/App.tsx](src/app/App.tsx) (~3100 lines). When making changes, `Grep` for the section-comment banners (`// ─── NAME ───`) to jump to the relevant part rather than reading the whole file. Sections in order: TYPES, CONSTANTS, INITIAL DATA, PERSISTENCE, CONTEXT, HELPERS, UI PRIMITIVES, IMAGE UPLOAD, AVATAR, PRODUCT DETAIL MODAL, LOGIN VIEW, NAVIGATION, RECEIPT, POS VIEW, INVENTORY VIEW, HISTORY VIEW, COMMISSIONS VIEW, USERS VIEW, BRANCHES VIEW, HEADER, APP PROVIDER + ROOT.

`src/app/components/ui/` holds the (mostly unused-by-App.tsx) shadcn/ui component library scaffolding generated by Figma Make — treat it as a component toolbox, not as things already wired into the app.

### State model

- Root state shape is `AppState { users, products, sales, commissionTiers, branches, logoUrl?, barcodeCounter, saleCounter }`, held in `AppCtx` (React Context) and set up in `AppProvider`. `saleCounter` (mirrors `barcodeCounter`'s pattern, both in the singleton `app_settings` row) drives sale folios: `POSView.confirmSale` mints `SALE-0007`-style zero-padded ids from `state.saleCounter + 1` instead of a timestamp, so folios read as a clean incrementing sequence to staff even though nothing else about a sale is sequential.
- `loadState()` (async, `GET /api/state`) and `saveState()` (fire-and-forget from the caller's perspective, `PUT /api/state`) are the *only* two functions that talk to the backend — every mutation handler across the app still just calls `setState((s) => { const ns = {...}; saveState(ns); return ns; })` exactly as before, so `saveState`'s internals could be swapped again without touching those ~30 call sites. `AppProvider` awaits `loadState()` in a `useEffect` on mount and renders a loading/error screen (with retry) until it resolves — nothing else in the tree can render before real data exists. A separate `moda_auth_v2` `localStorage` key still stores just the logged-in user id — that's session state, not business data, and intentionally wasn't moved to the DB.
- **`PUT /api/state` replaces the entire database on every call** (wipe + reinsert inside one transaction, in `server/db.mjs`'s `replaceFullState`) rather than doing granular per-entity updates. This mirrors how the app always treated persistence (one big blob, written wholesale) and avoids rewriting every mutation call site into REST calls, but it means: no optimistic concurrency / two browsers saving at once will clobber each other (last write wins), and every save re-sends the full catalog+sales+users. Fine at this app's scale; worth knowing before assuming any kind of partial-update or multi-writer safety.
- **`saveState` serializes its own PUT calls** (module-level `saveInFlight`/`pendingSaveState` in the PERSISTENCE section) — only one `PUT /api/state` is ever in flight; calls that arrive while one is running collapse into just the most recent state and get sent once the current one finishes. Without this, firing several mutations back to back (e.g. adding a few branches quickly) could send overlapping full-table-rewrite transactions that conflict in MariaDB (`ER_CHECKREAD`, "Record has changed since last read") and surface as a spurious `toast.error` even though the data was fine moments later. Don't remove the queue without another way to prevent that.
- **Branches** are admin-managed data, not a hardcoded list: `AppState.branches: string[]` (its own `branches` table, `name` as the primary key — see `server/db.mjs`) is what every branch `<select>`/filter/chip in the app iterates, replacing the old hardcoded `BRANCHES` constant. `BranchesView` (own nav item, admin-only) is the CRUD: create appends a unique name; rename cascades the old→new name across `users[].branch`, `sales[].branch`, `AppState.branchLogos`, and every product variant size's `stockByBranch` key (so historical sales and live stock stay attributed to the renamed branch, not orphaned); delete is blocked (via `toast.error`, no partial/silent state change) if any user is still assigned to that branch or if any variant size still has stock > 0 there, and always requires at least one branch to remain. `BranchLabel` (HELPERS-adjacent) renders a small set of hardcoded per-name colors (with a `-webkit-text-stroke` outline) for the four original branches; a branch created later with no matching entry just renders in the default text color — no code changes needed to add branches. Each branch can also have its own logo (`AppState.branchLogos: Record<branchName, url>`, `branches.logo_url` column) — uploaded per row from `BranchesView` via the same `uploadImage(file, "logos")` flow as the store logo; falls back to a plain `Store` icon anywhere it's shown unset.
- **Branch switching differs sharply by role.** Admin has an always-available branch `<select>` in `Header` (`changeBranch`, updates `users[].branch` + the local `user` immediately). Sellers instead get a **mandatory, once-per-actual-login** modal (`AppInner`, gated by `needsBranchSelect` — a plain `App()`-level boolean, deliberately *not* persisted) showing a 2-per-row grid of every branch's logo/name; it has no close button or backdrop-dismiss (`onClose={() => {}}`), so picking one is the only way past it, and changing branches after that means logging out and back in. The distinction between "just logged in" and "session restored from `localStorage` on page load" matters here: only `LoginView`'s `onLogin` (wrapped as `handleLogin` in `AppInner`) sets `needsBranchSelect`; the separate `currentUser` `useEffect` that restores an existing session on mount does not, so refreshing the page mid-session never re-prompts a seller who already picked. `warehouse` gets neither mechanism — fixed to whatever branch is set on their user record, same as before this feature.
- **Products** have nested `variants` (by color+model), each with a `sizes: VariantSize[]` array (`{ size, stockByBranch }`, where `stockByBranch` maps a branch name from `state.branches` to a quantity — a size can exist in some branches and not others). Total/branch-scoped stock is always derived via `sizeStockAt`/`sizeStockTotal`/`totalVariantStock`/`totalProductStock`, never stored flat. POS gates size selection and sale stock deduction by the seller's own `user.branch`; InventoryView's branch filter chips switch between a read-only all-branches breakdown and per-branch editable steppers.
- **Product form's variant builder** (inside InventoryView's `Editar producto`/`Nuevo producto` modal) uses one unified card style for both new and already-added variants — picking a Color + Modelo and pressing "Agregar" immediately creates an (initially empty) variant card, expanded, using the exact same UI a saved variant uses; there's no separate "new variant" panel anymore. Stock entry is a table per variant card: rows are tallas, columns are every branch in `state.branches` at once (`updateSizeStock(variantId, size, branch, stock)`), so an admin can fill different quantities per branch for a size in one pass instead of switching a branch selector per size. `save()` strips any variant left with zero tallas (an abandoned draft) and blocks saving with a `toast.error` if the Color/Modelo bar still has unsaved text in it — the fix for a real bug where filled-in fields silently vanished if "Agregar"/the final save was clicked in the wrong order.
- **Sales** embed a snapshot of `CartItem[]` (denormalized name/price/variant info). Sales no longer carry their own commission fields — commission isn't computed per sale anymore. `sale.subtotal`/`total` always stay as originally charged (an unaltered historical record); returns are tracked separately via `CartItem.returnedQty` and netted out on demand through `returnedAmount`/`netTotal`/`hasReturn` (HISTORY VIEW section) rather than by mutating the original totals.
- **HistoryView is a small container** (own `tab` state, not persisted) over two tabs — `DailySalesTab` ("Ventas por sucursal", default) and `TotalHistoryTab` ("Historial total", the original full search/filter/sort view). A seller only ever sees their own branch in the daily tab (no branch picker, no corte button) and their own sales in the total tab (unchanged prior behavior); only `user.role === "admin"` gets a "Todas las sucursales" combined option — `warehouse` is scoped like a seller for this page (branch-locked), even though it shares `TotalHistoryTab`'s edit/delete/devolución access with admin (`canManage = user.role !== "seller"`).
- **`TotalHistoryTab` CRUD**: admin/warehouse can edit a sale's administrative fields only (payment method, seller, branch — never items/quantities, so stock and commissions can't be silently desynced by an edit), delete a sale entirely (restocks whatever hadn't already been returned), or process a **devolución** — a partial, per-item return that restocks the returned quantity at `sale.branch` and increments that line's `returnedQty`, without deleting the sale record. The detail modal holds only the sale's `id` (`detailId`, not the `Sale` object) and re-derives the current sale from `state.sales` on every render — holding the object directly went stale the moment a nested edit/return/delete modal changed `state.sales`, since React doesn't retroactively update an old object reference.
- **`DailySalesTab` / "corte de caja"**: a **non-destructive, repeatable** snapshot — not a locking end-of-day close — of a branch's (or, admin + "Todas", every branch's) sales for the current calendar day up to the moment `Hacer corte` is pressed. Each press appends a `Corte` (own `cortes` table/`AppState.cortes`, no FK to `sales`) so staff can re-run it later the same day (e.g. a last-minute sale after an earlier cut) without anything being locked or overwritten; today's past cortes for the current scope are listed below and reopen the same printable summary. Beyond the aggregate counts/totals, each `Corte` also carries a **frozen itemized breakdown** (`sales: CorteSaleSummary[]` — folio, branch, net total, payment method, `"NxItem, MxItem"` label — stored as a `sales_snapshot` JSON column, not re-derived) so a corte's detail stays accurate forever even if the underlying `Sale` is later edited/returned/deleted by `TotalHistoryTab`'s CRUD; the summary modal groups this array by `branch` at render time, which is how the same code shows a flat per-sale list for a single-branch corte and a per-branch-grouped-with-subtotals list for a "Todas las sucursales" one. Mixed-payment sales keep their originally recorded `cashAmount`/`cardAmount` split unadjusted in the cash/card totals even if partially returned — apportioning a partial return across a cash/card split has no single correct answer, so this is a deliberate simplification, not a bug.
- **Commissions** are period-based, not per-sale: `AppState.commissionTiers` (`CommissionTier[]`, `{ min, max: number|null, percent }`) is a shared, admin-editable bracket table — a seller's *total* sales in a chosen window (1–6 weeks) lands in one bracket, and that bracket's `percent` applies to the whole total (not marginal/progressive). Each `User` has `commissionMode: "tiers" | "custom"` — `"custom"` bypasses the tier table entirely in favor of that user's own `customCommissionPercent`. All of this — viewing, editing tiers, and toggling a seller's mode — lives in `CommissionsView`, its own nav item/page; there's no commission UI left in `UsersView` or `HistoryView`.
- **Printed tickets (`ReceiptModal`'s and `DailySalesTab`'s corte-de-caja printable content) must use inline `style` props, never Tailwind classes.** `doPrint`/`printCorte` grab `printRef.current.innerHTML` and drop it into a bare popup window with no app stylesheet loaded — Tailwind classes on that content render fine on-screen (inside the real app) but do *nothing* once printed, since nothing defines them in the popup's `<head>`. This already happened once (a printed ticket came out as unstyled plain text) and was fixed by switching that content to the shared `tk` style-object constants (`tk.row`, `tk.hr`, `tk.bold`, etc., defined right above `ReceiptModal`) instead of `className`. If you touch either printable block, keep using `tk`/inline styles — don't reach for a Tailwind class there even if it looks fine in the browser preview.
- **Auth**: login is by **username**, not email — `User.username` (`users.username` column, `UNIQUE`, plain string like `"admin"`, no email-format validation) is what `LoginView`/`UsersView` collect and what `POST /api/login` looks up. `POST /api/login` (same `dataApiServer()` plugin) is the only place a plaintext password is ever compared — server-side, against a bcrypt hash in `users.password` (`server/db.mjs`'s `authenticateUser`). The client never receives password hashes: `getFullState()` omits the field entirely, so `User.password` is optional and only populated transiently when the client is *setting* one (new user, or a password change in `UsersView` — leaving it blank on an edit means "keep the current password"). Because `replaceFullState` deletes and reinserts the whole `users` table on every save (see above), it first snapshots existing hashes so an unrelated edit to a *different* user can't wipe everyone else's password — don't remove that snapshot step if touching `replaceFullState`.

### Image uploads

Product photos, user avatars, and the store logo are **real uploaded files**, not base64-in-`localStorage` — `uploadImage(file, category)` (HELPERS section) POSTs multipart form data to `/api/upload/{articulos|logos|usuarios}` and stores the returned `/uploads/...` URL string on the product/user/`state.logoUrl`. That endpoint is implemented as a Vite dev-server middleware (`uploadServer()` in [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts), using `multer`) which writes into `public/uploads/<category>/` and creates those folders on startup if missing. **This only exists while the Vite dev server is running** (i.e. `npm run dev` or the `frontend` Docker service) — `vite build` produces static files with no server behind them, so this upload flow has no production equivalent yet. `ImageUpload`/`AvatarUpload`/the sidebar logo control all show an uploading state and surface failures via `sonner` (`toast.error`, mounted as `<Toaster/>` in `App()`).

### Views & roles

Six views, gated by `UserRole` (`admin | warehouse | seller`) via `NAV_ITEMS` in the NAVIGATION section:
- `pos` (POSView) — product search/filter, cart, variant/size/qty selection, checkout, printable receipt.
- `inventory` (InventoryView) — product + stock management. admin/warehouse only.
- `history` (HistoryView) — past sales.
- `commissions` (CommissionsView) — period-based commission summary per seller, tier-table editor. admin only.
- `users` (UsersView) — user management. admin only.
- `branches` (BranchesView) — sucursales CRUD (create/rename/delete). admin only.

`App` → `AppProvider` (context) → `AppInner`, which shows `LoginView` when logged out, otherwise picks the active view from `VIEW_COMPONENTS` and renders `SideNav` (desktop) / `BottomNav` (mobile) + `Header` around it.

### Styling

Tailwind v4 via `@tailwindcss/vite` (see [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts)), with design tokens in [src/styles/theme.css](src/styles/theme.css) / [globals.css](src/styles/globals.css). UI is dark-mode-first, mobile-first with a `lg:` breakpoint split between mobile bottom-tab layouts and desktop split-panel/sidebar layouts (see POS view's `tab === "cart"` conditional rendering pattern, reused elsewhere).

### Figma Make conventions (don't remove)

- [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts) has a custom `figma:asset/...` resolver plugin — required for imports under `src/imports/`. Do not remove.
- The React and Tailwind Vite plugins must both stay even if a change looks like it doesn't need Tailwind.
- `vite.config.ts`'s `assetsInclude` should only ever add `.svg`/`.csv` — never `.css`, `.tsx`, or `.ts`.

## Docker (local dev)

`docker-compose.yml` runs three services for local development:
- `mariadb` (+ `adminer`) — schema in `docker/init/01-schema.sql` mirrors the `AppState` shape (`users`, `products`, `product_variants`, `variant_sizes`, `sales`, `sale_items`, `commission_tiers`, `branches`, `app_settings`). This is the app's real, active database — see "State model" above. `docker/init/02-seed.sql`'s `users.password` values are bcrypt hashes, not plaintext (comment in that file lists which demo password each one is). Note: `docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` scripts only run against a *fresh* (empty) `mariadb` data volume — adding/editing a table in `01-schema.sql` after the volume already exists (as when the `branches` table was added) requires applying the DDL by hand against the running container too (`docker compose exec mariadb mariadb -uroot -p"$MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD" ita_flores -e "..."`).
- `frontend` — built from `Dockerfile.dev`; installs deps at image-build time but bind-mounts the repo over `/app` (with an anonymous volume over `/app/node_modules` so the Linux-built modules aren't clobbered by the host's), so it's a hot-reloading dev server, not a production build. `vite.config.ts`'s `server.watch.usePolling` is required for file-change events to reach the container across the bind mount (especially on Windows/Docker Desktop) — don't remove it. This same container *is* the "backend": `server/db.mjs` (using `mysql2`/`bcryptjs`) is imported straight into `vite.config.ts` and mounted as dev-server middleware — there's no separate backend service/container. It reaches MariaDB via the `DB_HOST=mariadb`/`DB_NAME`/`DB_USER`/`DB_PASSWORD` env vars set on the `frontend` service (same credentials as the `mariadb` service, from `.env`), and `depends_on: mariadb: condition: service_healthy` so it never starts before the DB can accept connections.

`docker compose up -d` starts all three; the app is then reachable at `localhost:5173` same as running `npm run dev` natively — don't run both at once, they'll fight over the port.

**Adding a new npm dependency:** a plain `docker compose up -d --build frontend` is not enough — the anonymous `node_modules` volume from the previous container is reused as-is (stale), so the new package won't be there even though the image rebuilt. Use `docker compose up -d --build --force-recreate -V frontend` (the `-V` renews anonymous volumes) instead.

## To-Do (from 2026-08-27 security/architecture audit)

Ordered by severity. The root problem behind items 1-4 is the same: `/api/state` (GET/PUT in `vite.config.ts`) has no server-side auth at all — every role check in the app is enforced only in the React client and can be bypassed with a direct HTTP request.

- [x] **Critical — add real server-side auth to `/api/state`.** ~~`POST /api/login` doesn't issue anything the client can prove later; `AppProvider.login` just stashes `{id}` in `localStorage`. Anyone who can reach the dev server can `GET`/`PUT /api/state` with zero credentials.~~ Done (2026-08-27): `POST /api/login` now issues an HMAC-signed, HttpOnly `ita_session` cookie (`server/session.mjs`, stateless — no session table, 8h expiry) that `/api/state` and `/api/upload/*` verify via `requireSession()` before touching the DB/filesystem, 401 otherwise; `POST /api/logout` clears it. Needs `SESSION_SECRET` in `.env` (see `.env.example`) — the process throws on first use if it's missing. Because `/api/state` is now gated, `AppProvider` had to change how it boots: it can't preload full state before a login anymore, so `LoginView` now renders against a placeholder `EMPTY_STATE` and `login()` fetches the real state itself right after a successful `/api/login`, returning the `User` directly instead of a boolean. This still doesn't check *whose* session it is for authorization (item 2 below is still open — any logged-in user can still PUT a payload that edits another user's role/password).
- [x] **Critical — close the account-takeover hole in `replaceFullState`.** ~~Because `PUT /api/state` is unauthenticated, a caller can include a `password` field on any user object (e.g. `admin`) and `server/db.mjs`'s `replaceFullState` will hash and store it — or just flip that user's `role` to `"admin"`.~~ Done (2026-08-27): `replaceFullState(state, caller)` now takes the requester's session (`{id, role}`, from `requireSession` in `vite.config.ts`) and validates every row in `state.users` before touching the DB — throwing a new `ForbiddenError` (mapped to HTTP 403) otherwise. **`role`** may only be set/changed by an admin, full stop — deliberately *not* "the user themselves", since that's exactly the escalation being closed (a non-admin flipping their own `role`). **`password`** may be set by an admin or by that account's own owner (`caller.id === u.id`) — self-service is safe for a password, unlike a role. Creating a brand-new user (any row whose id isn't already in the `users` table) also requires admin, matching `UsersView` already being admin-only in the UI. Verified: self role-escalation → 403, setting another account's password → 403, self password change → 200, an unrelated save with no user changes → 200 (no false positives for routine saves), admin editing another user via the real `UsersView` UI → still works. Known remaining gap, not attempted here: because `PUT /api/state` still round-trips the *entire* `users` table on every save, a session that's gone stale relative to a very-recent admin role edit could still trip the 403 on an unrelated save — rare (role edits aren't routine) and it fails loudly (visible error) rather than the pre-existing silent last-write-wins clobber, but worth knowing. Other fields on a user row (branch, commissionMode, active, etc.) are still unauthorized-by-role — deliberately left open because `changeBranch` (a seller picking their own branch, and admin's branch switcher) is a legitimate non-admin self-edit of `users`; broadening this further belongs with item 3 below (general payload validation), not this fix.
- [x] **High — validate `PUT /api/state` payloads server-side.** ~~Right now `replaceFullState` trusts the client blob completely (negative prices/stock, arbitrary commission tiers, etc. all get inserted as-is).~~ Done (2026-08-28): new `server/validateState.mjs` (`validateState()`, throws `ValidationError` → HTTP 400) runs as the very first line of `replaceFullState`, before a DB connection is even taken from the pool. Checks types/required fields, enum membership (`role`, `gender`, `sizeSystem`, `paymentMethod`, `commissionMode`), and non-negative bounds on every price/stock/percent/counter field, plus a couple of structural invariants (sale must have ≥1 item, tier `max ≥ min`, no duplicate branch names). Deliberately *not* a full schema validator — doesn't check string lengths or cross-entity references (e.g. a sale's `branch` actually existing in `state.branches`), since the DB doesn't enforce those either and it wasn't what the audit flagged. Verified: a negative product price is rejected with 400 before touching the DB.
- [x] **High — fix the cross-session lost-update race.** ~~`saveInFlight`/`pendingSaveState` in `App.tsx` only serialize saves within one browser tab; two different sellers (or two tabs) saving near-simultaneously can silently clobber each other via the full-table-rewrite (`PUT` last-write-wins), losing a sale or an inventory edit.~~ Done (2026-08-28): optimistic concurrency via a `state_version` counter on the `app_settings` singleton row (`docker/init/01-schema.sql`, self-migrated into an already-existing DB by `ensureSchema()` in `server/db.mjs` — `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, since `docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` only runs on a fresh volume). `replaceFullState` does `SELECT state_version ... FOR UPDATE` inside the save transaction — this genuinely serializes two concurrent saves (the second blocks until the first commits) rather than racing — and throws `ConflictError` (→ HTTP 409) if the caller's `state.stateVersion` doesn't match, otherwise writes `currentVersion + 1` and returns it. Client-side, `App.tsx` tracks the confirmed version in a module-level `lastKnownVersion` (not threaded through React state / the ~30 `setState`-then-`saveState` call sites — `loadState()` sets it, `performSave()` reads it fresh on every call and updates it from the response), so chained saves within one tab keep working while a genuinely stale one 409s. On a 409, `performSave` shows a toast and reloads the page (no clean way to merge just one change into fresh server state from that generic a call site) — blunt, but correct: the loser's write is rejected instead of silently clobbering, which is what actually stops the oversell case (`confirmSale` computing stock off stale client state). Verified end-to-end with two concurrent `PUT`s at the same version: first succeeds (`stateVersion` 0→1), second gets a clean 409 instead of overwriting.
- [x] **High — stop trusting the upload `Content-Type` header.** ~~`uploadServer()`'s `fileFilter` in `vite.config.ts` only checks the client-supplied mimetype, so an `image/svg+xml` upload can contain `<script>` and serve as stored XSS when opened directly from `/uploads/...`.~~ Done (2026-08-28): `uploadServer()` now buffers to memory (`multer.memoryStorage()`) and sniffs actual magic bytes (`sniffImageType()`) before writing anything to `public/uploads/` — PNG/JPEG/GIF/WEBP only, chosen by signature, never by the client's mimetype or original filename. **SVG is no longer an accepted upload format at all** — sanitizing SVG (stripping `<script>`, event-handler attributes, etc.) is a much harder problem than just not accepting an inherently-scriptable format, and nothing in this app (product photos, avatars, logos) actually needs vector graphics. The saved filename's extension now also comes from the sniffed type, never from `req.file.originalname` (previously `path.extname(file.originalname)` — client-controlled). Verified: a `.svg` with an embedded `<script>`, even relabeled with mimetype `image/svg+xml`, is rejected with 400; a real PNG uploads and is served back correctly.
- [ ] **Medium — rate-limit `POST /api/login`.** No attempt limit today; `authenticateUser`'s good practice of not distinguishing "unknown user" from "wrong password" is undermined by unlimited brute-force attempts.
- [x] **Medium — remove the hardcoded demo credentials from `LoginView`** ~~(`admin/admin123`, `almacen/almacen123`, `vendedor/vendedor123`, shown directly on the login screen)~~. Done (2026-08-28): the whole "Cuentas de demostración" block removed from `LoginView`. The seed accounts themselves still exist in `docker/init/02-seed.sql` (bcrypt-hashed, fine for dev seed data) — this was specifically about not advertising the passwords on-screen.

The `frontend` service's `5173` was deliberately left as-is (binds all interfaces) — that's intentional per the existing `server.host: true` comment in `vite.config.ts`, for reaching the app itself from other devices. Verified via `docker compose ps`: mariadb shows `127.0.0.1:3306->3306/tcp`.
- [x] **Low — no tests, lint, or typecheck configured.** ~~Worth adding at least a typecheck script given `App.tsx` is ~3100 lines and easy to silently break.~~ Done (2026-08-28): added `typescript`, `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom`, `@types/node`, `@types/multer` as devDependencies, a `tsconfig.json`, and `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`). Scoped to `App.tsx`, `main.tsx`, and `vite.config.ts` (which pulls in `server/*.mjs` via `allowJs`) — deliberately **excludes** `src/app/components/ui/`, the shadcn scaffold CLAUDE.md already flags as "mostly unused-by-App.tsx", so the check tracks the real app instead of drowning in errors from code nothing calls. Fixing it to a clean pass caught real issues, not just noise: **`setVSize(sys.sizes[0])` in the product form's size-system picker referenced a setter that doesn't exist anywhere in `InventoryView`** — a genuine `ReferenceError` waiting to fire the first time someone changes the size system while creating a new product (removed; nothing needed it, sizes are re-derived from `form.sizeSystem` elsewhere via `sizesForSystem`). Also fixed: `Btn`'s `onClick` type was too narrow (declared `() => void` but the click event is real and used at 4 call sites — was silently unsound, not a runtime bug, since the type just didn't match what was actually passed through to the native `<button>`); `Input` was missing a `max` prop despite being passed one (the write-off-quantity field's native spinner/validation silently had no upper bound — the `onChange` clamp still caught the actual applied value, so not a data bug, just a UX gap); a `.catch()` handler's return type leaked into `performSave`'s declared `Promise<void>`. Also surfaced (not fixed — out of scope, flagged for whoever picks up that feature): `Corte.fondoAmount`/`entradas`/`salidas` are declared but never populated by `DailySalesTab.doCorte()`, and their data source (`AppState.cajaFondos`/`cajaMovimientos`) is never read or written anywhere — a cash-float-tracking feature whose data model exists but whose UI/logic was never finished. Made those three fields optional to reflect that honestly rather than fabricate fake `0` values into what's supposed to be an immutable historical snapshot.

System Guidelines

Use this file to provide the AI with rules and guidelines you want it to follow.
This template outlines a few examples of things you can add. You can add your own sections and format it to suit your needs

# General guidelines

Any general rules you want the AI to follow.
For example:

* Only use absolute positioning when necessary. Opt for responsive and well structured layouts that use flexbox and grid by default
* Refactor code as you go to keep code clean
* Keep file sizes small and put helper functions and components in their own files.

# Design system guidelines
Rules for how the AI should make generations look like your company's design system

Additionally, if you select a design system to use in the prompt box, you can reference
your design system's components, tokens, variables and components.
For example:

* Use a base font-size of 14px
* Date formats should always be in the format "Jun 10"
* The bottom toolbar should only ever have a maximum of 4 items
* Never use the floating action button with the bottom toolbar
* Chips should always come in sets of 3 or more
* Don't use a dropdown if there are 2 or fewer options

You can also create sub sections and add more specific details
For example:


## Button
The Button component is a fundamental interactive element in our design system, designed to trigger actions or navigate
users through the application. It provides visual feedback and clear affordances to enhance user experience.

### Usage
Buttons should be used for important actions that users need to take, such as form submissions, confirming choices,
or initiating processes. They communicate interactivity and should have clear, action-oriented labels.

### Variants
* Primary Button
  * Purpose : Used for the main action in a section or page
  * Visual Style : Bold, filled with the primary brand color
  * Usage : One primary button per section to guide users toward the most important action
* Secondary Button
  * Purpose : Used for alternative or supporting actions
  * Visual Style : Outlined with the primary color, transparent background
  * Usage : Can appear alongside a primary button for less important actions
* Tertiary Button
  * Purpose : Used for the least important actions
  * Visual Style : Text-only with no border, using primary color
  * Usage : For actions that should be available but not emphasized
